consensus.text: There should be a "community economy" the way there is a creator economy, that is recognized and resourced
A robust community enterprise means listening to people and adapting based on their needs.
Not a must but nice to have: impact measurement for their groups, data collection. This could also be beneficial for grant applications
We need to help people outside the Community community understand the benefit of Community.
It's difficult to find truly affordable NYC venues for private member events.

representativeStatements.text: I spend more time on logistics (marketing, outreach, finding venues, making materials, follow-up) than on the actual community work I care about.
I would do this work full-time if I could financially.
NYC should create a fund that pays community builders directly for the time they put in, not just reimburses event costs
The administrative side of community work (insurance, permits, legal, payments) is or would be a real barrier for me.
I spend more time on logistics (marketing, outreach, finding venues, making materials, follow-up) than on the actual community work I care about.
A peer network of other community builders would matter more to me than a one-off grant.

topStatements.label: Highest agreement
topStatements.text: There should be a "community economy" the way there is a creator economy, that is recognized and resourced

topStatements.label: Most divided
topStatements.text: Philanthropy, not government, is the most realistic source of sustained support for community work in NYC.

topStatements.label: Most engaged
topStatements.text: Community builders should be paid for their work, not just reimbursed for expenses.
